ch37.d.beta: Relative speed of the two frames, $\beta = v/c$
ch37.assume.units: Units: $c = 1$; lengths in light-seconds (ls, the distance light travels in 1 s), times in s
ch37.c.goal.dilate: A moving clock runs slow: $\Delta t = \gamma\,\Delta t_0$. $\Delta t_0$ is the proper time (the tick interval measured in the clock's rest frame), $\Delta t$ the interval measured in a frame where the clock moves, $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - \beta^2}$ the Lorentz factor (at least 1)
ch37.c.goal.mutual: The effect is mutual: in each frame the other frame's clock runs slow
ch37.c.obs.zigzag: Moving light clock: the light runs a slanted zigzag at the same speed $c$, so each round trip takes longer
ch37.c.obs.count: The number on a clock counts its round trips (ticks); the clock at rest counts faster
ch37.c.obs.both: From S the S′ clock is slow; from S′ the S clock is slow. Neither frame is special
ch37.c.assume.clock: Mirrors $D$ = 1 ls apart, so a clock at rest ticks every $\Delta t_0$ = 2 s (its proper time). A moving clock that leaves the view comes back on the other side
ch37.l.goal.contract: A moving rod is shorter along its motion: $L = L_0/\gamma$
ch37.l.goal.mutual: The proper length $L_0$ is measured in the rod's rest frame; the effect is mutual
ch37.l.obs.short: The rod's tick marks shrink by the same factor
ch37.l.obs.both: From S the S′ rod is short; from S′ the S rod is short
ch37.l.obs.beta: Lengths across the motion (the rod's thickness) do not change
ch37.l.assume.rod: Both rods have proper length 4 ls, marks every 1 ls of proper length
ch37.d.d.mode: Effect read off the diagram: a moving clock, a moving rod, or the order of two events
ch37.d.d.grid: S grid (grey, solid) and S′ grid (orange, dotted: lines of constant $x'$ and $ct'$)
ch37.d.goal.axes: The S′ axes look tilted in S: the $ct'$ axis has slope $1/\beta$, the $x'$ axis slope $\beta$, symmetric about the light path (45°)
ch37.d.goal.read: Read time dilation $\Delta t = \gamma\,\Delta t_0$ and length contraction $L = L_0/\gamma$ directly off worldlines and lines of simultaneity
ch37.d.goal.order: Two events inside each other's light cone (timelike) keep their order in every frame; outside it (spacelike) the order can change
ch37.d.obs.dilate: Time dilation: the $ct'$ axis is the worldline of the S′ clock ($x' = 0$); orange ticks mark every 1 s of $ct'$. The S line of simultaneity (blue dashed) through E ($ct'$ = 2 s = the proper time $\Delta t_0$, one light-clock tick) meets the $ct$ axis at $ct = \gamma \times 2$ s
ch37.d.obs.ticks: Ticks on the tilted axes: the orange ticks on the $ct'$ axis (1 s apart) sit $\sqrt{(1+\beta^2)/(1-\beta^2)}$ times farther apart on the diagram than the ticks on the $ct$ axis (1 s apart), 1.46 times at β = 0.6. The $x'$ spacing of the S′ grid has the same factor. Distances on the diagram have a different scale in each frame
ch37.d.obs.contract: Length contraction: the green strip is the world strip of a rod at rest in S′ (proper length 3 ls), its solid green edges the world lines of the rod's ends. Cut along the S line of simultaneity its length is $L = L_0/\gamma$ (blue, F to R); cut along the S′ line it is $L_0$ (orange, F to R′)
ch37.d.obs.order: Event order: drag B. Inside the grey wedge between the $x$ and $x'$ axes, B comes before A in one frame and after it in the other ($\Delta t$ and $\Delta t'$ differ in sign); the wedge always lies outside the light cone
ch37.d.obs.light: The light cone (grey dashed) is the same in both frames: light moves at $c$ in every inertial frame
ch37.d.assume.terms: Terms: an event is something that happens at a definite place $x$ and time $t$, one point of the diagram. A worldline joins the events an object passes through (vertical for an object at rest). A world strip is the band formed by the worldlines of all points of an extended object. A line of simultaneity joins events at the same time in one frame (S: parallel to the $x$ axis, S′: parallel to the $x'$ axis). The light cone is the worldline $x = \pm ct$ of light sent both ways from an event (two 45° lines in a one-dimensional diagram); inside it is timelike, outside spacelike
ch37.d.assume.origin: The origins coincide ($t = t' = 0$ at $x = x' = 0$)
ch37.d.assume.objects: The S′ clock is at rest at $x' = 0$, the rod at rest from $x'$ = −3.5 to −0.5 ls; the rod is cut at event F at $ct'$ = 2.5 s; event A is fixed at the origin
ch37.s.goal.relative: Two events simultaneous in one frame are not simultaneous in another
ch37.s.goal.c: Light moves at $c$ in both frames, which is why the arrival times differ
ch37.s.obs.train: Train frame (bottom): the flash starts at the centre and reaches both ends at the same time
ch37.s.obs.ground: Ground frame (top): the rear end moves toward the light and the front end away from it, so the rear is reached first
ch37.s.obs.dt: The ground-frame time difference is $\Delta t = \gamma v L_0/c^2$, larger for larger β
ch37.s.obs.diagram: The two arrivals are simultaneous in the train frame and 4 ls apart: a spacelike separation (outside the light cone), so their time order depends on the frame (spacetime diagram tab, event order)
ch37.s.assume.train: Train proper length 4 ls; the flash goes off at the centre ($x = x' = 0$) at $t = t' = 0$; the light is absorbed at the ends; ground posts are 1 ls apart in S and $1/\gamma$ ls apart in the train frame (length contraction)
